body.x: Seongnam City, led by Mayor Shin Sang-Jin, announced the successful opening of the Seongnam Pavilion at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, which runs from January 7 to 10 (local time). To support the global expansion of Seongnam’s SMEs and startups, the city sent its largest-ever delegation of 41 companies and hosted the pavilion’s opening ceremony.

The Seongnam Pavilion’s opening ceremony occurred at 1:30 p.m. on January 7 on the second floor of the Venetian Expo’s Global Pavilion. Although Mayor Shin Sang-Jin could not attend due to economic constraints, the ceremony was led by Eui-Jun Lee, Director of the Seongnam Industry Promotion Agency, and Fred Jung, Mayor of Fullerton, where the Seongnam Business Center (K-SBC) is located. Key invited buyers were also present.

During the ceremony, Eui-Jun Lee emphasized, “By sending our largest-ever delegation of 41 companies to CES 2025, Seongnam is actively supporting the global expansion of our SMEs and startups. The Seongnam Pavilion represents a valuable opportunity and a strong foundation for Seongnam companies aiming for the global market. The city will continue to support innovative companies as they expand into international markets.”
The Seongnam Pavilion, featuring 25 SMEs and startups, showcased advanced technologies in artificial intelligence (AI), healthcare, smart cities, and mobility.

body.x: Notably, three Seongnam-based companies—Sky Labs Inc., BrainU Co., Ltd., and ANDOPEN Co., Ltd.—received the CES Innovation Awards, showcasing the city’s technological prowess and competitiveness on the global stage.

Sky Labs was recognized for its CART VITAL (project “Apollon”), a monitoring solution for multiple vital signs such as oxygen saturation, irregular pulse, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and body temperature, tailored for home and care institutions. BrainU was awarded for its VET CAI, an EEG-based animal anesthesia depth monitor. ANDOPEN earned recognition for SNAPPASS, its next-generation two-factor authentication solution based on facial recognition.

To support local companies participating in CES 2025, Seongnam City provided systematic assistance, including support for award application fees, booth rental and installation costs, airfare, transportation of goods, on-site interpretation, and promotional activities.
Seongnam City stated, “We will continue to provide unwavering support to help local companies establish competitiveness in the global market.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
